extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators and research teams preparing an ERC Synergy (SyG) grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing and structuring an ERC Synergy (SyG) proposal and what the ERC evaluation panels look for across the three-stage review (extended synopsis/B1, full proposal B1+B2, interview). Focuses on interdisciplinarity, keywords/abstract, PI contributions, and interview presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 evaluation: extended synopsis and PI track record (Part B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extended synopsis, alongside the CVs of the PIs and their corresponding track records (part B1 only), are evaluated by at least three reviewers out of a single panel comprised of panel members and chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a remote assessment, SyG panel chairs and vice-chairs meet and select the proposals that are fit to pass to Step 2. The number of selected proposals at this step is up to seven times the indicated budget for the call of that year. Emphasize a clear, compelling extended synopsis and strong PI track records in B1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocking period for Step 1 rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs whose proposals are rejected at this point may be subject to a blocking period, depending on the evaluation score at this step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that poor scoring in Step 1 can trigger a submission restriction; invest effort into the B1 materials to avoid a blocking period.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC keywords selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to select 4-6 ERC keywords out of a given list alongside free keywords that best describe their project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the 4–6 ERC keywords and free keywords that most accurately represent your project topics because these are used to indicate necessary expertise and help allocate your proposal to appropriate reviewers/panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract should present interdisciplinary aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should present the interdisciplinary aspects of the project and focus on the different fields it comprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the abstract to signal the interdisciplinary scope and conceptual novelties; the abstract helps panels identify the fields involved and the expertise required for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 evaluation: full proposal (Parts B1 and B2) by panels and external reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete version of the selected proposals (Parts B1 and B2) is evaluated by the panel members as well as by external specialized reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five new panels (each 15–18 experts) are formed from the Step 1 pool to cover the proposals' specific topics; following remote individual assessment and panel discussion, proposals are shortlisted to approximately four times the indicative budget allocated per panel. Ensure B2 contains the detailed substantiation of the ideas presented in B1.

rubrics_metrics.name: No restriction on resubmission after Step 2 rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals that have reached Step 2, no restriction on further submission is applied upon rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected at Step 2, teams can revise and reapply; use reviewers' feedback to improve the full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition is dynamic to cover interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels’ composition is dynamic and subject to change in order to fit the multidisciplinary nature of the proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because panels are adjusted to match proposal topics, carefully chosen keywords and a clear abstract will influence which experts assess your application; anticipate that reviewers may come from multiple disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 interview: mandatory PI presence and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs of the retained proposals are invited to an interview with 3–5 panels (possibly altered as compared to Step 2) where the presence of all PIs is obligatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews usually last around 45 minutes; applicants may be given 10–15 minutes to present, with the remaining time for Q&A. Prepare a concise, engaging presentation and be ready for detailed questioning from multiple panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview criterion: demonstrate scientific intrigue and synergy
rubrics_metrics.description: During the interview, applicants may be given 10–15 minutes to present their research project. PIs are expected to scientifically intrigue the reviewers while demonstrating the synergistic nature of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the presentation and Q&A to show how the collaboration produces added value beyond individual contributions, emphasizing integrated objectives, methodologies, and outcomes that cross disciplinary boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear description of each PI's contribution and budget alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The contribution of each PI to the overall collaborative work should be reflected in the budgetary considerations and in the conceptual and operational aspects of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make roles, responsibilities, and resource allocations explicit in the proposal (and during interview) so reviewers can assess the feasibility and fairness of the collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking determines funding (priority order subject to available funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that meet the demanding requirements of the ERC and are recommended for funding will be financed if sufficient funds are available. Projects will be funded in priority order based on their rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to maximize your rank by addressing all evaluation expectations (quality of synopsis, PI track record, interdisciplinarity, detailed B2, and interview performance) because funding is competitive and limited.
